The world's catch, 2018

Which countries produce the most fish, and how much of it is farmed?

length ∝ total_fisheries_t (log scale — the top value is 1,292× the median) · depth ∝ capture_t (log scale — the top value is 281× the median) · 199 rows · drag to turn · scroll to zoom · click for the row

199 rows · 0.287 GB scanned trust 100/100
SQL
SELECT
  country_code,
  ROUND(MAX(IF(indicator_code = 'ER.FSH.PROD.MT',  value, NULL))) AS total_fisheries_t,
  ROUND(MAX(IF(indicator_code = 'ER.FSH.CAPT.MT',  value, NULL))) AS capture_t,
  ROUND(MAX(IF(indicator_code = 'ER.FSH.AQUA.MT',  value, NULL))) AS aquaculture_t,
  ROUND(MAX(IF(indicator_code = 'ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS',  value, NULL)), 2) AS marine_protected_pct
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
WHERE indicator_code IN ('ER.FSH.PROD.MT','ER.FSH.CAPT.MT','ER.FSH.AQUA.MT','ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS')
  AND year = 2018
GROUP BY country_code
HAVING total_fisheries_t IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY total_fisheries_t DESC
LIMIT 300

Insights

China alone lands 81.0M tonnes — 45% of the world total of 178.5M — and 82% of it is farmed, not caught. Aquaculture is not a supplement to Chinese fishing; it is Chinese fishing.

aquaculturechina2026-08-20
from “Which countries produce the most fish?”

Peru is the counter-example: 7.3M tonnes, 1.4% farmed. It sits fifth in the world on a single wild fishery (anchoveta), which is why its output swings with El Niño in a way China's does not.

captureperu2026-08-20
from “Where has aquaculture overtaken the wild catch?”

Protection and production are close to unrelated: the US protects 41.1% of its waters and lands 5.8M tonnes, while Indonesia protects 3.1% and lands 22.0M. Across 199 countries the two measures correlate at r = -0.03.

protection2026-08-20
from “Which countries protect the most of their own waters?”

Read the protection number with the indicator's definition in hand: ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS is protected marine area as a share of TERRITORIAL waters, while the protected area itself can extend into the EEZ beyond them. That is why Slovenia reports 213.4% — not an error to filter out, but the reason a 'share of the sea' reading of this column is wrong. Monaco (99.8%) and New Caledonia (96.6%) sit just under the same ceiling.
